To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) Threshold voltage changes in MOS transistors can be modeled as a function of total dose and gate length.
threshold voltage shifts increase as gate length decreases.

the threshold voltage shifts after total dose exposure are larger for shorter gate lengths and that the threshold voltage changes for parasitic transistors are more sensitive to total dose than for MOSFETs with gate oxides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of total dose radiation on the threshold voltages of CMOS devices.
the total dose radiation effects on the electrical performance of CMOS devices.
the total dose response of CMOS devices and its relation to scaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the total dose hardness of MOS devices is a function of gate oxide, field oxide, and gate lengths and is a strong function of gate oxide and field oxide thicknesses.
the total dose hardness of MOS devices will be significantly affected by CMOS scaling.
scaling of the gate length of CMOS devices can have a significant impact on total dose radiation hardness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the total dose hardness of a CMOS circuit can be significantly degraded as a result of scaling of CMOS gate length and field oxide thicknesses.
scaling of CMOS device gate lengths can result in decreased total dose hardness for both gate oxide transistors and parasitic field oxide transisters.
the total dose hardness of a CMOS circuit is determined by the weakest transistor in the circuit and that the weakest transistor is the field oxide transistor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
total dose radiation effects on CMOS circuits are not only dependent on the gate oxide, but also the field oxides.
scaling of the gate oxide is not sufficient for total dose hardness.
scaling of the channel length of CMOS devices can result in increased radiation hardness.
